newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soy products end with solid gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soy products end with solid gains.

text.p: Nearby CBOT soy product futures surged higher in late trade, rallying in tandem with the soybean market, traders said.
Moderate commodity fund buying in May soybeans pushed that contract through buy-stop orders at $7.91 per bushel and spurred the late rally.
Before the close, trade in soyoil and soymeal had been choppy and lackluster for most of the session, traders said.
Some weakness in soymeal was tied to falling cash basis levels. Prices were too high for most end-users, who were buying only on an "as-needed" basis, dealers said.
Export business for soymeal and soyoil has also been slipping as buyers begin to turn to South American soyoil and soymeal to meet forward and spot needs.

Traders also characterized the U.S.'s slowing crushing pace as supportive to the soy products. The National Oilseed Processors Association put the weekly crush rate at 29.970 million bushels versus last week's pace of 30.864 million.
Soyoil futures settled up 0.10 to 0.22 cent per pound, with May up 0.16 at $24.65. Soymeal settled down $4.00 to up $3.80 with May up $3.40 at $254.70 per ton.
On the day, LIT America bought 400 lots May soymeal and 100 lots March. Smith Barney sold 300 lots May and Rosenthal Collins sold 200 lots March and 100 May, floor sources said.
In soyoil trading, Cargill sold 300 lots May, 200 lots September and 200 lots March. Rosenthal Collins bouight 200 lots October, trade sources said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 32,000 contracts, below the 42,233 traded Thursday.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 28,000 contracts, sharply below the 46,571 traded Thursday.
